title: Leading Chinese mathematicians unite behind use of AI in research
source_used: Shanghai Daily, as hosted by City News Service (citynewsservice.cn, byline Yang Meiping, 11 Oct 2026), plus BigGo Finance's account of the same launch; the SCMP original returned HTTP 403
key_facts: The Yau Laboratory Alliance for Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence was officially launched at Tsinghua University on Sunday 11 Oct 2026, led by Fields Medal winner Shing-Tung Yau.
It integrates eight Chinese mathematical research institutions and assembles a 1,000-strong research team (BigGo Finance says nearly 1,000).

Founding members are in Beijing, Shanghai, Nanjing, Shenzhen and Hong Kong, including Tsinghua's Qiuzhen College and the Yau Mathematical Sciences Center; headquarters are in Beijing's Haidian District, whose local authorities pledged support.

Stated aim: develop homegrown AI models for mathematical research; six priorities include open public infrastructure for AI-assisted mathematics, AI interpretability and security, links to quantum computing and life sciences, talent training and a flagship journal for AI-assisted mathematics.
Yau said properly handled AI would be 'epoch-making' but poorly managed it could bring 'catastrophic consequences', particularly for China's science and technology sector.
Yau said the past half year has brought unprecedented upheaval to research because AI produced many pivotal results in a short span.
BigGo Finance, reporting the same launch, says it comes against the backdrop of OpenAI's release of 722 mathematics manuscripts on GitHub, and that the journal is expected to launch in early 2027.
Shanghai Daily reports no funding figure and no delivery date for a model.
quote_evidence: China's higher education sector has further advanced interdisciplinary mathematics and artificial intelligence research, as the Yau Laboratory Alliance for Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence was officially launched at Tsinghua University on Sunday.
Led by Fields Medalist professor Shing-Tung Yau, the alliance integrates eight top Chinese mathematical research institutions and assembles a 1,000-strong research team.

Established to pool elite academic talent nationwide, the alliance unites 1,000 professional mathematicians across member institutions to develop China's homegrown AI models dedicated to mathematical research, thereby driving nonlinear, leapfrog progress in related fields, he added.
why_it_matters_hint: A large organised group of Chinese mathematicians commits to building AI for mathematics, in a month when AI-made proofs have split the field.
notes: SCMP (the curator's item) returned HTTP 403, so its text was not read; the same launch was read at Shanghai Daily (via City News Service, whose URL path is 'shanghaidaily') and BigGo Finance. Source is therefore Shanghai Daily, the outlet whose own reporting we read. The OpenAI backdrop comes from BigGo only; Shanghai Daily does not mention OpenAI. Our 7 Oct 2026 edition carried The Verge's report on the 722 manuscripts (item 77).
